page: Amazon Web Services r9gd.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server powered by custom AWS Graviton arm64 processors running at 3.3 GHz. The hardware delivers 192 dedicated physical cores configured with one thread per core. By providing a bare-metal deployment model without a hypervisor layer, the instance eliminates virtualization overhead and thread-scheduling contention, ensuring direct access to the physical processor architecture.

The system is equipped with 1,536 GB of memory, maintaining an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage capabilities include 11,400 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local instance store volumes, delivering high-speed block storage directly connected to the system bus. Networking is supported by a 100 Gbps baseline interface, allowing high-throughput node-to-node communication and fast data movement across distributed environments.

From an efficiency perspective, the high density of dedicated arm64 cores coupled with 1.5 TB of memory and integrated NVMe capacity offers a consolidated platform for resource-heavy services. The absence of discrete GPUs and the use of the arm64 instruction set require software compatibility for ARM execution environments. The server is suited for large-scale in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, relational database hosting, and high-throughput data processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r9gd.metal-48xl is a bare-metal memory-optimized instance powered by AWS Graviton arm64 processors running at a base clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The server exposes 192 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, bypassing hypervisor layers to avoid resource contention across concurrent threads. It integrates 1,536 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8 GB per core allocation suited for large working sets. For high-speed data handling, the configuration includes 11,400 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local storage, granting direct access to low-latency disk arrays without network storage overhead. Network throughput is backed by a 100 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance contains zero discrete GPUs, focusing entirely on high core density, extensive RAM capacity, and high-bandwidth local input-output operations. This architecture is designed for memory-heavy enterprise databases, distributed in-memory caches, large data mining applications, and extract, transform, load pipelines requiring high memory per thread.
